text:
kelly_support: FYI acme reported streaming failures to their private inference endpoint in our Private deployment. Small responses OK, but long-running streaming requests get RST after ~10s. Can infra take a look?

sam_acme_sre: Repro steps I ran: 
1) curl -v --http2 --no-buffer "https://10.2.5.14/v1/stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"
Observed: first chunk arrives, then connection resets. curl output: 
* Connected to 10.2.5.14 (10.2.5.14) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/2
< HTTP/2 200
< content-type: text/event-stream

[data chunk]
* Received reset from peer
* Closing connection 0

I also captured a short tcpdump on the client side: 
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.2.5.14 and port 443 -c 50 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
Inspection of the pcap shows a TCP RST coming from 10.2.5.14 -> client_ephemeral_port immediately after the second chunk.

kelly_support: Thanks, that's helpful. We suspect a firewall/NACL/SG issue — typical pattern when a stateless NACL blocks the high ephemeral return port.

ryan_infra: Quick checklist: are you using a custom network ACL on the subnet hosting the inference nodes or the NAT/egress subnet? Remember: security groups are stateful (return traffic allowed automatically) but NACLs are stateless and require explicit rules both directions. If an allow exists for 443 outbound but the NACL blocks inbound ephemeral 1024-65535, the server's TLS response packets will be dropped and you see RSTs. :thinking:

Commands to run on your side for triage: 
- tcpdump on the client and on the inference host: 
  sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and host 10.2.5.14 and port 443' -w /tmp/side-a.pcap
  sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and port 443' -w /tmp/side-b.pcap
- Check conntrack on Linux host (if applicable): sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.2.5.14
- Quick curl reproduce: curl -v --http2 --no-buffer https://10.2.5.14/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'

Also check VPC Flow Logs for the timeframe to see DENY on ephemeral ports. If you have an appliance (FW / proxy) in the path it may be cutting long-lived connections after an idle timeout.

priya_runtime: Additional notes from runtime side: our inference runtime uses long-lived HTTP/2 streams and keeps KV caches per connection. This means we expect the TCP/TLS session to remain open for many seconds to minutes. Middleboxes that re-write or terminate TLS (TLS-inspection) or aggressively drop high-port ranges will break streaming. Two concrete fixes we usually ask customers to apply: 
1) If there's a custom NACL on the subnets between client <-> inference, add both inbound & outbound allow for TCP ports 1024-65535 (ephemeral) to/from the other subnet or 0.0.0.0/0 for testing, then narrow to Redwood IPs/ENIs once verified. 
2) If there's a firewall appliance, add a rule to allow established TLS sessions and increase inspection idle timeout to > 300s or disable session termination for Redwood traffic.

Sample AWS NACL rules (temporary test): 
- Inbound: rule 100 allow TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0 ALLOW
- Outbound: rule 100 allow TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0 ALLOW
(Then test and remove wide-open rules once satisfied.)

If you prefer not to edit NACLs, confirm that all traffic from inference nodes to your clients flows through a security-group-backed path (no stateless NACL in between).

kelly_support: One more thing — if you're NATting egress through a managed gateway, ensure the NAT gateway's subnet NACLs also allow ephemeral ranges both ways. NAT idle timeouts can also drop connections; if you suspect NAT, we can try a keepalive/heartbeat test.

sam_acme_sre: We opened ephemeral 1024-65535 both inbound and outbound on the NACL for the inference subnet as a test. After that, streaming connections stayed up and all chunks arrived. Confirmed fix on our side. Thanks for the clear repro notes. :thumbsup:

ryan_infra: Great — thanks for verifying. For follow-up: narrow the NACL to the minimal CIDR(s) that cover the client subnets or Redwood peer ranges, then keep monitoring. Also consider adding TCP keepalives from your client (or our runtime can send pings) if appliance timeouts are unavoidable.

priya_runtime: Filed a runtime note to add troubleshooting doc links to the private onboarding guide (streaming + network requirements) so customers hit this sooner.

kelly_support: Closing loop with acct team. sam_acme_sre — let us know if you want us to review the exact NACL rule IDs before you tighten them back up.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1043 (support ticket linked)

sam_acme_sre: Appreciate it — we'll reach out if anything else crops up.
